summaryEn: Teaches you to put a pay claim in the subjunctive, together with your reasons.
Teaches you to discuss risk against return with the conjunction of proportion.
Teaches you to set out a business plan with conditional conjunctions.
Teaches you to discuss official formalities in nominal, formal language.
Teaches you to draw a line and to describe balance with clauses of purpose.
Teaches you to talk about making contacts, with the stand-ins for the passive.
Teaches you to describe a risky decision with a conjunction of contrast.
Teaches you to talk about an uncertain future with subjective modals.
Teaches you to discuss the terms of a second job with genitive prepositions.
Teaches you to defend a costly pursuit with relative clauses of possession.
Teaches you to build comparisons that are not real, with als ob.
Teaches you to tell degrees of certainty apart with dürfte, müsste and könnte.
Teaches you to say how body language has its effect, with a clause of means.
Teaches you to name a misunderstanding with als ob and to put it right.
Teaches you to discuss putting things off and pushing past it, with the stand-ins for the passive.
Teaches you to describe how a habit is built and how it is broken.
Teaches you to describe putting yourself in someone else's place, in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to set out the rules of a fair debate with two-part conjunctions.
Teaches you to name the unreal standards you set yourself, with als ob.
Teaches you to talk about change with conditional conjunctions and the language of courage.
Teaches you the fixed patterns and the skeleton of formal writing.
Teaches you to put a request for information politely, in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to weigh up quotes and to decide with reasons.
Teaches you to draw information out with indirect questions at the end of an interview.
Teaches you to close a presentation with a summary, a conclusion and a look ahead.
Teaches you to build a short farewell speech with the past behind the past.
Teaches you the formal, participle-heavy language of a letter of reference.
Teaches you to describe being caught between two places, with als ob.
Teaches you to assess your own level and to make a plan with a target.
Teaches you to sum up the road travelled, with the past passive.
Teaches you to build the fixed phrases where the verb gives way to a noun, in formal language.
Teaches you to use the function verb phrases that institutional language leans on most.
Teaches you to voice an objection without losing the other side.
Teaches you to sense from the particles the gap between what is said and what is meant.
Teaches you the distanced, nominal language of a corporate crisis statement.
Teaches you to open a subject, to take on risk and to ask for something in return.
Teaches you to steer without giving orders, in the language of suggestion and support.
Teaches you to understand the set phrases of office German and to use them when you need to.
Teaches you to build the rhetoric that convinces in a short space of time.
Teaches you to report both sides impartially and to look for common ground.
Teaches you the work the particle doch does: inviting, insisting and pushing back.
Teaches you the particle ja for surprise and the particle mal for softening a request.
Teaches you the tone of accepting what cannot be changed, with eben and halt.
Teaches you to say something without being sure, with the particle wohl.
Teaches you the soothing, comforting tone the particle schon carries.
Teaches you to judge the dose of impatience and warning that particles carry.
Teaches you the culture of saying little and meaning much, and how to use it.
Teaches you to keep a conversation flowing with particles and ready-made phrases.
Teaches you to build the most polite forms of request on the phone.
Teaches you to use particles together and in the right order.
